name: Victoria: one dwelling on a lot, General Residential Zone
version: Victoria Planning Provisions at amendment VC322 (gazetted 2 November 2026): clauses 54 and 32.08; National Construction Code 2022, ABCB Housing Provisions; Livable Housing Design Standard 2022
about: The numerical standards for one dwelling on a lot, as a survey read them on the date above (research/literature/reports/Design of a single building.md, §8). They were not checked clause by clause against the published text, the scheme is amended often, and a schedule to the zone or an overlay can change a standard: read the clauses before relying on a finding.
applies: Clause 54 applies where a permit is required, which for one dwelling is a lot of less than 300 m². A larger lot falls under Part 5 of the Building Regulations 2018, whose values differ on open space and overshadowing.
not_evaluated: The street setback where a dwelling abuts: the lesser of its setback and 6 m (54.02-1). The 4 m stated here is for a street with no abutting dwelling; set your own.
Walls on boundaries: an average height of 3.2 m (54.02-4); only the greatest height of 3.6 m is found.
Tree canopy and deep soil (54.02-6), the front fence (54.02-7).
The seclusion and least width of private open space (54.03-2); its solar access (54.03-3).
Daylight to new windows from a space clear to the sky (54.03-4).
What depends on the neighbours: daylight to their windows (54.04-1), their north-facing windows (54.04-2), overshadowing (54.04-3), overlooking (54.04-4), their solar panels (54.05-2).
Rooftop solar area (54.05-3), the shading of north windows (54.05-4), car parking (52.06).
Energy: the 7-star rating and the whole-of-home rating (NCC H6D2).
